entities.summary: Alfonso Carrillo de Acuña was a Spanish politician and Roman Catholic archbishop who played a crucial role in the governance of Spain during the late Middle Ages. Born in 1413 in Carrascosa del Campo, he rose to prominence as a diplomat and administrator under King Ferdinand II of Aragon. Appointed as Archbishop of Zaragoza in 1452, de Acuña worked tirelessly to promote the Catholic faith and maintain stability in the region. His efforts contributed to the unification of the Spanish kingdoms and laid the groundwork for the eventual conquests of Granada and the Americas. De Acuña's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Catholic Church on Spanish society and politics, as well as his role in shaping the country's early modern identity. He died on July 10, 1482, leaving behind a lasting impact on the course of Spanish history.
